newsitem.title: ITALY: Two arrested in Venice Fenice theatre fire inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Two arrested in Venice Fenice theatre fire inquiry.

text.p: Two men were arrested on Thursday in connection with an investigation into a fire that destroyed Venice's historic La Fenice opera house last year, judicial sources said.

Investigators at first said the January 29, 1996 blaze was most likely caused by a short circuit but later their suspicion turned to arson. There were no further details immediately available of the arrests.
Considered an architectural jewel with its gilded and tiered interior, La Fenice held priceless memories as the stage for premieres of some of Italy's most famous operas.
The city has vowed to rebuild the opera house at a cost of at least $100 million.
Last June, Italy's lower house of parliament approved an initial 20 billion lire ($13 million) of government funds for reconstruction.
Music lovers from around the world also have pledged money to rebuild the theatre.
La Fenice, which means The Phoenix in English, first opened in 1792 and was rebuilt after a fire in 1836.
